sources.title: Arduino Nano 3.x pinout
sources.ref: docs.arduino.cc/hardware/nano: D0-D13, A0-A7, 5V, 3V3, GND, VIN, RESET; PWM on D3, D5, D6, D9, D10, D11; A6 and A7 are analog input only; board 45 mm by 18 mm

sources.title: ATmega328P DC characteristics
sources.ref: DS40002061: same logic ratings and brownout as the Uno. Active supply 0.010 A at 5 V and 16 MHz, read from the active-current figure

sources.title: CH340G
sources.ref: WCH CH340 datasheet: USB working current 0.012 A

sources.title: Power LED
sources.ref: 1 kohm series resistor on the board photograph. Forward drop 1.8 V assumed, so 0.0032 A at 5 V

sources.title: USB diode S4
sources.ref: Vishay SS12-SS14, document 88746, Fig. 3. The clone marks this diode S4. No polyfuse and no P-MOSFET

sources.title: C106
sources.ref: 10 uF, 16 V tantalum on +5V after the diode. Position assumed. ESR 5 ohm assumed, inside the 4-8 ohm maxima of a case-A part of that rating (Kemet T491, AVX TAJ)

sources.title: D13 LED resistor
sources.ref: 1 kohm assumed. The resistor code on the board is unknown

sources.title: D13 input leakage
sources.ref: DS40002061 Iin 1 uA max. A 5 Mohm resistor from D13 to ground, so the LED node has a DC path while the pin is an input

sources.title: Reset network
sources.ref: Arduino Nano 3.x schematic (A000005): 10 kohm from RESET to +5V, and 100 nF from the USB-bridge DTR pin
